9965.text: Whether new governors write a pause into state rules.

qu5h.text: This is Tech Signal, where we pick today's real signal out of all the noise.

32a2.text: Today's topic: a surprise big issue in the US midterms, AI data centers.

qwhy.text: Wait, isn't a data center just a building full of computers? Why are Americans voting to block it?

cvea.text: We'll save that for the main topic. First, yesterday's tech news, November 4.

czez.text: OK. According to The Verge, ChatGPT can now make animated GIFs directly.

p33d.text: Yes. Type a line or drop in a photo, and it makes one.

y8lz.text: edit it frame by frame, then share it.

wg8u.text: It launched with a new image model; reportedly, it's open to all ChatGPT and Codex users.

tww7.text: OpenAI also says it now makes over 4 billion images a week, up from 3 billion in September.

hobm.text: The report doesn't give length, resolution or file size. Check OpenAI's own docs first.

8edi.text: From images it makes to sounds that get recorded.

7spw.text: According to TechCrunch, on Tuesday Apple began testing audio AI features for Apple Watch in a developer beta.

uv3k.text: Four. Detecting key sounds like doorbells and alarms, and identifying songs.

ydfk.text: The other two record. Live Rewind replays what was said in the last 15 seconds;

6lr8.text: Siri Recaps summarizes your whole day's audio and saves it as notes.

sa4f.text: A TechCrunch writer tried it for a day. At the car shop, the clerk talked fast; it caught the deductible and repair timeline.

nwlu.text: But it also logged pointless small talk. The writer says if the talk were more private, it'd feel invasive.

siria.text: If set to always run, yes. TechCrunch says Apple processes as much as it can on the device,

h8e0.text: doesn't identify who's speaking, and keeps no raw audio.

ra54.text: What bothers some people is tech always listening, slowly becoming normal.

p6v0.text: Can regular people use it now?

hh4z.text: Not yet. It's only in the developer beta, for Apple Watch Series 12; the report doesn't say when it officially launches.

sr4v.text: From AI on your wrist to AI that writes code.

56da.text: According to TechCrunch, Meta has bought AI coding startup Conductor.

ajeb.text: It lets you run several AI agents at once, each in its own workspace, splitting one software project.

7ynj.text: Did Conductor build those agents itself?

1qd0.text: No. TechCrunch says the agents come from big labs like Anthropic and OpenAI.

4jol.text: The founder says the cloud service shuts on the 20th of this month, then users' cloud data gets deleted.

f3o4.text: Other core features keep working until early next year.

ccjq.text: Meta confirmed the deal to TechCrunch, but gave no price or terms.

boit.text: From coding AI to AI in the classroom.

9s0f.text: Per TechCrunch, Google told schools Tuesday: Gemini can be shut off;

wxj7.text: but turn off the other AI features, and Search goes too.

z66e.text: Google Search now has AI Overviews and a conversational AI Mode, hard to separate from search itself.

pt89.text: After criticism, Google said Gemini and the search features are off by default; schools pick what to enable.

14z5.text: Right. DuckDuckGo's CEO posted a guide showing schools how to make it their default search engine.

5u57.text: It stresses its AI can be turned off, too. That's its own claim.

a35h.text: So it's using the moment to recruit.

vt5z.text: TechCrunch cites figures Google released earlier: about 50 million Chromebooks in schools,

eid1.text: and over 150 million Google Classroom users. But that's not how many are affected this time.

kzgt.text: The report doesn't split it by region; each school's admins set it up.

5jfg.text: From school policy to national policy.

4fhs.text: According to TechCrunch, OpenAI's chief global affairs officer posted that the 2028 US election could be a pivotal moment for AI.

uvh3.text: Interesting timing. TechCrunch says his post came right after the Democrats' big midterm wins.

w6mf.text: The author, Lehane, likens AI's economic impact to the 1930s New Deal, and lays out five areas,

3o19.text: from worker protections and education to AI safety and data centers.

0i9h.text: Yes. Reportedly, he warned that politicians backing a pause on new data centers could put America's lead over China at risk.

v9p7.text: TechCrunch asked OpenAI more; no reply by press time.

j9ct.text: That word, data center, is going to keep coming up today.

99uy.text: With all this AI agent news, is anyone actually using them? Today's signal number.

numa.text: Four rides. Uber said on its earnings call yesterday that third-party AI agents booked only that many in all of Q3.

cbj0.text: Yes, a whole quarter. Delivery is a bit higher: about 500 orders in Halloween week. But the periods differ, so don't compare them directly.

csbh.text: Some experts fear people will send AI agents to book rides and order food, and never open Uber.

q4fg.text: The Verge thinks this number shows that risk is still small.

yvbf.text: So sending an AI agent to call your ride is still a long way off.

fhyn.text: AI agents barely get used yet, but the buildings behind AI are already being blocked by ballots.

i2a5.text: Imagine you live in Janesville, Wisconsin. On Tuesday, you get your ballot.

vota.text: One question: before any big development on the old General Motors plant site, should everyone vote again?

x4e0.text: And data centers fit in how?

4dqz.text: According to Decrypt, that land is linked to a proposed data center. The result: over 60% voted yes.

terq.text: In plain terms: what is a data center, really?

w24t.text: A building packed with chips and servers. Every question you ask an AI gets computed in a place like that.

gslf.text: Decrypt cites The Washington Post: on Tuesday, voters in at least 29 US places backed banning or limiting data centers.

9gmv.text: But why? Doesn't everyone use AI?

wggb.text: Electricity. Decrypt says data centers use so much power that residents worry about higher bills and strain on the grid.

4qk5.text: and development deals lacking public oversight.

j8kn.text: You use AI and it feels far away, in the cloud. But the cloud is really a building near someone's home.

hkoq.text: The Verge cites an NBC News Election Day poll: 76% of voters surveyed oppose a data center in their own community.

nfom.text: Depends who's counting. Decrypt cites election data site Ballotpedia: 41 measures in 10 states, and in 28 of them, a yes vote means limits.

olgz.text: The Verge uses another tally: of 45 local ballot measures, by Wednesday morning 33 had results that would limit development.

atya.text: In Hubbard, Ohio, over three quarters backed banning data centers.

oq86.text: The town of Wells, Maine, put a 180-day pause on large data centers.

9snz.text: A city in Kansas barred data centers using over 10 megawatts for ten years.

tbsc.text: Any asking the other way, to support them?

dov8.text: Yes. Of Ballotpedia's 41, another 13 would allow or support data centers.

0xoa.text: Like Joliet, Illinois: nearly 80% of voters rejected an advisory measure for AI data centers.

b8ht.text: Even asking to support them got voted down.

advq.text: So those places can't build now?

adva.text: Not necessarily. Decrypt says some are just advisory votes, voicing opinion; passing doesn't automatically halt work.

mrdo.text: Then there are states. In Texas, the Democratic candidate beat the sitting governor.

y4hj.text: She campaigned on pausing new data centers.

rd7c.text: Decrypt thinks wins like this could bring tougher state-level rules.

xnxr.text: So data centers decided the election?

5zz0.text: The Verge cautions: it's hard to credit any one win directly to this issue. Some who backed modest limits also won.

monq.text: Who wins, who loses? And the money?

8mfi.text: Most directly, developers. The Verge says they now face a harder place to build.

su43.text: Even winners who don't back a pause set other terms.

e351.text: Like a Republican winner in Florida, proposing developers pay their own energy and water;

fcxn.text: Iowa's winner, like the opponent, agreed to end tax breaks;

m1tz.text: Pennsylvania's governor signed an executive order banning nondisclosure agreements in data center projects.

ifrg.text: Decrypt says some are lobbying harder, some doing PR, like OpenAI, which wants to call data centers compute campuses.

c25g.text: Meanwhile, in yesterday's news, chipmaker Qualcomm is betting its growth on AI data centers.

kffj.text: Qualcomm? Don't they make phone chips?

24fy.text: Because of phones, exactly. The Verge says smartphone sales are down about 20% from 2025.

k5se.text: Qualcomm forecasts $15 billion in data center revenue by 2029,

ncun.text: eventually about 30% of its business. These are all the company's own forecasts.

q2gi.text: So voters blocking data centers could hurt Qualcomm?

mona.text: Reports don't say that; we won't infer it. But data centers that chips bet on must go somewhere.

twnq.text: Chips and data centers sound very relevant to Taiwan. Do the reports mention it?

twna.text: Honestly, no story today mentions Taiwan; we won't force it.

vgq2.text: One link we can see is memory.

o8a8.text: The Verge writes that AI data centers keep buying up the world's memory, causing shortages and pricier tech products.

upfl.text: So buying a PC gets hit too?

28yk.text: The Verge says the shortage already makes big memory upgrades hard for many.

bbfv.text: How long? Intel expects at least until next year;

yb2l.text: memory maker SK hynix says it could drag on until 2030.

rq0j.text: If the US builds fewer, is memory easier to buy?

omt0.text: The sources don't say; we won't guess. Whether Asia's supply chain is hit, no answer today either.

9dal.text: First, which votes are binding, and which are just statements.

v8ir.text: Third, who ends up paying for power, water and tax breaks.

2a7u.text: Real policy hinges on later laws and enforcement; The Verge gives no timeline.

7m2b.text: The one OpenAI's post was about?

yqj3.text: Right. TechCrunch thinks if voters worry about power bills and losing jobs to AI, AI becomes a bigger issue.

bbtv.text: Back to that Janesville ballot. It asked about just one plot of land, one building.

z2uw.text: But there's more than one ballot like that.

dum4.text: Right. Add up those 29 places, and AI's infrastructure became a question on the ballot.

tlgt.text: Voters have spoken. What do industry and critics say?

mg2t.text: Three quotes, word for word from the reports.

k97z.text: He said: if this country imposes some kind of moratorium, we'll fall into a recession.

wvgr.text: Brennan of the AI Now Institute, on OpenAI's post.

sy2z.text: She called it ahistorical at best, and harmful at worst.

ymgf.text: She sees a private company advocating policy for its own benefit.

syf4.text: It ties to the signal number. Uber's CEO says it's still very, very early.

8tfq.text: He also said Uber will make sure it doesn't depend on any single player.

sqnb.text: Uber says it's early; but once AI agents can touch money, the banks are already nervous.

jg1n.text: Yes. According to Decrypt, the US currency regulator OCC released its first AI framework for banking yesterday.

zrmc.text: It oversees banks. This 22-page framework is written for examiners, the people who assess how banks use AI.

o5cu.text: Not how powerful the AI is, but three things: what happens if it errs,

oqrx.text: and how much control humans keep.

mt7a.text: Top of the risk list: fully autonomous payment agents and real-time credit decision systems.

vory.text: More dangerous than a very powerful model?

ofxn.text: Yes. The OCC thinks a simple agent that can start transactions may be riskier than an advanced model that only writes internal documents.

x0l1.text: Safeguards: circuit breakers that halt it if things go wrong;

61wf.text: Right. Also caps on actions within a time window;

8vru.text: tighter permissions, and a kill switch.

yqdl.text: For context, Decrypt cites Axios: banks found unauthorized third-party AI agents operating in customer accounts.

tvdn.text: Morgan Stanley is blocking outside agents; JPMorgan, Bank of America and Citi are limiting access.

5l7f.text: But the OCC didn't tie the framework directly to these incidents.

c2tl.text: No. The OCC stresses it's not a new rule; it has examiners assess AI with existing risk categories.

xk39.text: Back to Wall Street. Per Decrypt, Morgan Stanley said Tuesday

suq6.text: it turned US stocks and Treasuries into blockchain tokens through a new DTCC service.

ftzx.text: America's securities depository and clearing company. Its DTC handles custody and settlement after trades, holding over $114 trillion.

jk7p.text: DTCC says no: same ownership and investor protections as the original securities, and they can be swapped back.

lwdi.text: Not yet. It's for qualified financial institutions; 20 have signed up, including Bank of America, Citi and JPMorgan.

r6no.text: Decrypt says this is a bank-led approach, unlike crypto firms launching their own tokenized stocks.

pdn6.text: So Wall Street's doing it itself.

7zu7.text: Money flows to tokens; some firms shrink.

t7ie.text: According to Decrypt, Circle, issuer of the USDC stablecoin, disclosed in its Q3 earnings that it cut about 5% of its staff.

to9e.text: Actually, net income rose 5% year over year.

oaq5.text: But its biggest revenue source, interest on the assets backing USDC, fell 8% as rates dropped.

elrc.text: Circle says it's to fit the organization to its operating model and strategic focus, but didn't say how many or which teams.

7kus.text: No. Decrypt lists crypto firms like Coinbase and the Ethereum Foundation that cut staff this year, citing a weaker market, AI, or both.

952e.text: Per Decrypt, Coinbase blogged yesterday that last week's Binance hack missed it.

5zbr.text: How does it say it's safer?

4dbk.text: It says over 99% of customer assets sit in offline cold storage.

8w63.text: Private keys are split up, never fully rebuilt when signing;

0eaj.text: and a sudden surge in withdrawals gets held for manual review.

dp9t.text: Can't say that. These are all Coinbase's own claims, relayed by Decrypt, not an outside assessment.

7duu.text: The rules for AI agents touching money are taking shape, and work is being reshuffled. And a reminder: no prices in this segment.

5eze.text: OK, practical. After all this news, what can we do today?

bcyl.text: These three are the show's suggestions, not instructions from Apple, Conductor or the banks.

8ijm.text: First, our advice: with any AI feature that records or summarizes, figure out when it's listening.

bxwm.text: Like that TechCrunch writer, wanting it off at night?

12sb.text: Right. At home or in private talks, we suggest turning it off; and you can give people nearby a heads-up.

e3d0.text: Second, if you or your team use Conductor's cloud, remember that date?

9nmu.text: We suggest saving what you need before then.

sope.text: Right, so save what you want to keep before the 20th.

2grf.text: Third, our advice: before letting AI tools touch your accounts, check you can set limits and revoke access anytime.

b3nx.text: From money to the absurd: today's noise. As election-night votes were counted, what was Sam Altman doing?

6r21.text: The Verge says he was defending his take on PC memory.

5ivw.text: On an interview show, he said people keeping limited memory in their own computers and using it only 5% of the time is pretty bad.

ynxd.text: He said he was taken out of context, and told a user: I hope you get tons of memory; we'll build more.

u1h0.text: But aren't data centers the ones grabbing memory?

ec2i.text: Right. So the spat is noise, but the shortage behind it is real.

1bip.text: My take: what matters most today is the data centers in this election.

ctww.text: Because AI isn't just an app; it has buildings and uses power, and the people next door are speaking with their ballots.

me8s.text: Industry and OpenAI are already responding.

gzox.text: So will data centers really get built slower?

txb8.text: Honestly, I'm not sure. Many votes are just statements, causation is hard to prove; it depends on the laws ahead.

qftg.text: The topic's full rundown is on Mokaair; link in the description.

qans.text: The answer: power bills, water and noise brought cloud AI to people's doorsteps.

0vcg.text: Near your home: yes or no? Tell us.
